items.title: Mild Weekend Gives Way to Sub-Zero Overnight Lows as Cold Snap Grips Mississauga and the GTA
items.summary: According to Environment Canada, a mild and sunny weekend across the GTA is giving way to a sharp cold snap this week, with overnight lows dropping below zero by Monday night. The agency says Sunday night will turn cloudy with a chance of showers, with lows around 5 C in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Oakville and Burlington. Monday will stay mostly cloudy with gusty winds up to 50 km/h and daytime highs ranging from just 7 C in Hamilton to 9 C in Toronto and Mississauga, forecasters say. Skies are expected to clear Monday night as the real cold moves in, with lows falling to minus 4 C in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Hamilton and wind chills as low as minus 9 in those areas. Oakville and Burlington will see milder lows near minus 2 C, the agency says. Tuesday and Wednesday are expected to stay sunny but cold, with highs of just 3 C to 4 C across most of the region.

items.title: Cocaine Tops the List as Dixie Road Emerges as Mississauga's Drug Trafficking Hotspot
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police data, 54 drug trafficking incidents were recorded across Brampton and Mississauga between Oct. 22 and Nov. 22, with 19 of them in Mississauga. Cocaine trafficking was the most common offence, accounting for 13 incidents force-wide. Police say heroin, other opioids and cannabis possession for sale each accounted for nine incidents, while methamphetamine trafficking made up another eight. In Mississauga, police say Dixie Road saw seven incidents, more than any other street in either city. Brampton streets including Steeles Avenue and Archibald Street each had four incidents, with three more spread across Peel Centre Drive, Gillingham Drive and Eastern Avenue. Peel police note drug trafficking carries a potential sentence of up to life in prison, depending on the drug and circumstances.

items.title: Surveillance Began Days Before Fatal Shooting of Mississauga Man in Botched Arrest, Inquest Hears
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, Peel police began watching the 28 year old Mississauga father days before officers shot and killed him. Det. Jason Sweeting told the inquest surveillance started after a tip alleged Francique had a firearm and was trafficking drugs. Officers never corroborated that tip, Sweeting said, though they believed Francique had breached a bail condition tied to earlier drug and gun charges. The plan, according to Sweeting, was to arrest Francique near his car once he left his townhouse, where he lived with his mother and stepfather, his bail sureties. An officer fatally shot Francique in the head during the arrest, and Sweeting testified everyone's safety was considered beforehand. The inquest, mandatory under the Coroners Act, is examining his death and may issue recommendations to prevent similar outcomes.

items.title: Dense Fog Cuts Visibility Across GTA Highways as Environment Canada Issues Warning
items.summary: According to Environment and Climate Change Canada, a weather warning covering a broad stretch of southern Ontario took effect Sunday morning as areas of locally dense fog formed near Lake Ontario. The agency says the fog is reducing visibility for motorists across Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Oakville, Burlington and Hamilton. Officials say the fog is expected to dissipate later in the morning as conditions improve. The weather agency warns travel will likely be hazardous in some locations because of the reduced visibility. Motorists are advised to turn on their vehicle lights, slow down and keep a safe following distance from other vehicles. Drivers should also be ready for sudden changes in visibility along highways near Lake Ontario. The warning affects some of the region's busiest corridors, including the QEW, Highway 403 and Highway 401, according to the agency.

items.title: ZoRaw Chocolates Turns to Pricier Whey Sources After Tariffs Hit Its U.S. Supply Chain
items.summary: According to CTV News Toronto, Mississauga chocolate maker ZoRaw Chocolates is contending with rising cocoa prices and a 50 per cent tariff on the whey protein it imports from the United States. Founder Gigi Gill told the outlet she started the low-sugar, high-protein chocolate company about five years ago after being diagnosed as diabetic and pre-diabetic. The company's Mississauga facility produces roughly 30,000 bars a day in flavours including milk, dark, almond and mint, sold in 4,000 stores nationwide including Costco and Loblaws. Gill says whey protein isolate is one of several ingredients Canada cannot supply domestically, forcing her to rely on American suppliers now facing Ottawa's counter-tariff. Switching suppliers is not simple, she says, since the ingredient needs specialized processing equipment and a long matching process.

items.title: Black creatives at Brampton conference vow to transform future of arts industry
items.summary: A group of Black creatives met in Brampton over the weekend to re-envision how they can strengthen the arts sector for Black artists.

items.title: Northern Ontario Braces for 20 cm of Snow While GTA and Niagara Get a Mild, Sunny Sunday
items.summary: According to Environment Canada, while northern Ontario braces for up to 20 centimetres of snow, the GTA and Niagara region are set for an unseasonably mild and sunny Sunday. The forecaster says Saturday night will stay clear across the region, with patches of fog developing overnight. Lows are expected to dip to around 5 C in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington, and 7 C in Durham and Niagara. Environment Canada forecasts a high of 14 C for Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington, with Durham reaching 15 C and Niagara warming to 16 C under south winds. Clouds are expected to move in Sunday night, bringing a 30 per cent chance of showers to most areas. The agency says winds will shift northwest overnight, gusting as high as 50 km/h in the western GTA. Drivers are warned to watch for fog early Sunday morning, which could reduce visibility on roads.

items.title: Hurontario Street Shut Down for Hours After Two-Vehicle Crash Leaves Woman with Serious Injuries
items.summary: According to Peel police, a woman was taken to a trauma centre with serious injuries after a two-vehicle crash in Mississauga on Saturday afternoon, Nov. 21. Police say a male driver involved in the same crash was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries. Southbound Hurontario Street was closed between Eglinton Avenue and Elia Avenue while officers investigated, according to police. Drivers were asked to seek alternate routes during the closure. Police have not said what caused the crash or whether charges are expected. Hurontario Street is one of Mississauga's busiest roads, running north to south through the city, and the Eglinton intersection is one of its main crossings. Police are asking anyone with information or dashcam footage to contact them and quote occurrence number PR260394750, or reach Crime Stoppers anonymously.

items.title: Mississauga Arts Council Honours Billy Talent for 15 Years Backing Mental Health Charity Make Music Matter
items.summary: According to CBC Peel, the Mississauga Arts Council presented Billy Talent with an award this week recognizing the punk rock band's work beyond its music career. The council says the honour reflects the band's long-running support for Make Music Matter, a mental health charity the group has backed for 15 years. CBC Peel reports the charity uses songwriting as a therapeutic tool meant to empower and help heal people. Host Nav Nanwa covered the recognition for CBC Peel. The award highlights local artists whose community contributions extend past their creative output, according to the broadcaster.
